#Moderation
this is a type of analysis were a variable (third variable) affects the strength of the relationship between two other variables (outcome and predictor).

`lm (outcome ~ predictor * moderator, data = dat)`

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(starwars)
```

##Question 1: doees sex moderate the realtionship between height and mass?
```{r}
lm1 <- lm(mass ~ height * sex, data = starwars)
```

```{r}
library(ggeffects)
a <- ggpredict(lm1, terms = c("sex"))
plot(a)
```

##Question 2: Does birth year moderate the relationship between mass and height
```{r}
lm2 <- lm(mass ~ height * birth_year, data = starwars)
summary(lm2)
```

```{r}
b <- ggpredict(lm2)
plot(b)

library(interactions)
interact_plot(lm2, pred = height, modx = birth_year)
```

# Mediation
```{r}
library(mediation)

```
 
mediation occurs where there is seemingly a relationship between x and y. In reality x predicts a mediator that in turn predicts y.
 
preacher and Hayes created a new approac that removed soem of the issues with Baron and Kenny. This is shown in the mediator package.
need to create two models:
1) predict the mediator from x
2) predict y from the x and the mediator

##Question: does birth_year mediat the relationship between height and mass.
```{r}
starwars2 <- na.omit(starwars)
lma <- lm(birth_year ~ height, data = starwars2)
lmb <- lm(mass ~ birth_year + height, data = starwars2)

med <- mediate(lma, lmb, treat = "height", mediator = "birth_year")
summary(med)
```
=Interpretation:
total effect: tells the relationship between x and y (indirect and direct effect)
ADE: average direct effect X -> Y
ACME: Average causal mediation effect X -> mediator -> Y

#Logistic Regression
linear regression with a dichotomous (binary) outcome

`glm(outcome ~ predictor, data = dat, family = "binomial"`

```{r}
data("mtcars")
summary(glm(am ~ mpg, data = mtcars))
```

#Linear mixed effects models/Repeated Measures ANOVA

## repeated measures ANOVA
repeated measures anova can be used when we have an outcome that is measured at multiple time points.
```{r}
data(sleep)
a1 <- aov(extra ~ group + ID, data = sleep) #this would but not totally correct
summary(a1)

a2 <- aov(extra ~ group + Error(ID), data = sleep) #error ID allows us to say that there are variables that are due to random error and error due to repeated subjects
summary(a2)
```

```{r}
library(ez)
ezANOVA(sleep, dv = extra, wid = ID, within = group)
```

##Linear mixed effects modeling

```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
```

use `lmer()` to create mixed effect
include `(Slope | Intercept)` in model
- (1 | variable) indicates random intercept, where participants may have different starting points
- if you replace the one with a second variable, it. indicates a random slope, were rate of change may differ across participants.
```{r}
data("ChickWeight")
lmer1 <- lmer(weight ~ Diet + (Time|Chick), data = ChickWeight)
summary(lmer1)
```

## Generalized linear mixed effect models (glmer)
`glmer(DV ~ IV + (slope | intercept ), data = dataframe, family = "")
-family options include binomial (dichotomous data) and poisson (count data)
